body: For petitioner: Abdul Samad Khattak edvocate. For respondent: Muhammad Ishaq Khattak advocate. **** ( SABIT ULLAII KIIAN. J.--- Through the instant civil revision, preferred under Section 115 ofthe Code ofCivil Procedure, 1908 ('CPC'), the petitioners have called in question the judgment and decree dated 23.70.2025' rendered by the learned Additional District Judge-III, Karak, whereby their Regular Civil Appeal No. 02i13 of 2025 was dismissed and the summary judgment and decree dated 07.12.2024 of the learned Civil Judge-IV, Karak, dismissing their Civil Suit No. 3917 of 2023 under Order XV-A CPC for want of jurisdiction, was maintained.

2. Succinctly stated, the facts giving rise to the instant petition are that the petitioners/plaintiffs claim to be co-owners in possession of the property comprised in Khata No. 19, Khasra No. 1085, measuring 05 kanals 08 marlas, situated in Mouza Karak (hereinafter "the

(SB) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah Khar @ Versus suit property"). Their case, as pleaded, is that the said Khasra number was carved out of old Khasra No. 250 in the settlement of 1974-75 and was handed over to the predecessor-in-interest of the respondents/defendants for the limited purpose of cultivation, but was erroneously entered a second time in the record of. 197 4- 75, reflecting the respondents as owners thereof. The petitioners assert that they are the original owners of the suit property, whereas the predecessor of the respondents had purchased a separate and distinct area measuring 28 kanals 04 marlas in the Shamilat in the year 1915. Their earlier suit, bearing No. 37/1 of 2027, was withdrawn with permission to institute a fresh suit vide order dated 12.05.2023 of the learned Civil Judge- II, Karak. The petitioners thereafter instituted the present suit for declaration, perpetual and mandatory injunction and ejectment of tenants, praying for a declaration to the effect that they are the owners of the suit property, that the respondents are their tenants, and that the entries to the contrary are wrong and ineffective qua their rights. Respondents No. 1 to 8 and 10 to 12 contested the suit, whereas the remaining respondents were proceeded against ex parte. Upon issuance of notice under Order XV-A CPC, the learned trial Court, without framing issues or recording evidence, summarily dismissed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 07.12.2024, holding that the relief claimed pertained merely to the borrection of revenue record, the jurisdiction in respect whereof stood barred under Section 172(2) of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Land Revenue Act, L967, and to the ejectment of tenants, which was triable under the Khyber Pakhtunl<hwa t @

(SB) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah Khan J Tenancy Act, 1950. The appeal preferred by the petitioners met the same fate vide the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.10.2025; hence, the instant revision petition.
3. Arguments of learned counsel for the parties have been heard and the record has been perused with their able assistance.

4. The sole question which falls for determination is whether the suit of the petitioners was barred under Section L72 of.the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Land Revenue Act, 1967 ("the Act of 1967"), or under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tenancy Act, 1950 ("the Act of 1950"), so as to warrant its summary dismissal under Order XV-A CPC.

5. It is by now well settled that the question whether a civil Court has jurisdiction to entertain a suit is to be determined, at the threshold, on the averments made in the plaint and the reliefs claimed therein. A bare reading of the plaint in the instant case reveals that the suit is not one merely for correction of entries in the revenue record. The petitioners lay claim to title over Khasra No. 1085 as its original owners and assail the entries of the settlement of L974-75 recording the respondents as owners, whereas the respondents, who stand recorded as owners, resist that claim. The real controversy between the parties is, therefore, one of title. The correction of entries and the ejectment sought are only consequential to the principal relief of declaration of ownership. The nature of a suit is to be determined from its substance and the principal relief
(SB) Honble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah Khan.
{ @ claimed therein, and not from the consequential reliefs appended thereto; nor can the form in which the reliefs are couched be permitted to override the substance of the claim.

6. Under Section 9 CPC, the civil Courts are vested with plenary jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature, excepting suits of which their cogtrizance is either e:gressly or impliedly barred, and a provision ousting such jurisdiction is to be construed strictly and is not to be readily inferred. Section L72 of the Act of 1967 bars the jurisdiction of the civil Court only in respect of matters which a Revenue Offrcer is empowered to dispose of under the Act, such as the preparation and maintenance ofthe record ofrights and the correction of entries therein. It does not oust the jurisdiction of the civil Court to determine questions of title. On the contrary, Section 53 of the Act of 1967 expressly provides that any person aggrieved by an entry in a record of rights or in a periodical record as to any right of which he is in possession may institute a suit for declaration of his right under the Specific Relief Act, 187?. In Rasta Mal Khan and others v. Nabi Sarwar Khan and others (1996 SCMR 78), the Hon'ble Supreme Court ofPakistan held that the exclusion ofjurisdiction relates to the correction of entries made by a Revenue Offrcer in the performance of his duty without touching the rights of persons in land, and that where such entries interfere with the rights of a person in land, he has to approach the civil Court for a declaration under Section 53 of the Act or Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. More recently, in Abdullah and others v' Waryam and others (2026 SCMR 1042), the Hon'ble
(SB) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah KIan.

( @ Supreme Court has held that the decisions of the revenue hierarchy are administrative and tentative in nature and neither determine the title ofthe parties nor resolve disputed facts; that a controversy as to title or the validity of the record requires evidence and falls within the jurisdiction ofthe civil Court under Section 9 CPC; and that the jurisdiction of the civil Court is barred only in respect of the matters specifically provided for in Section 172 ofthe Act.

7. This Court has consistently adhered to the same view. In Muhammad Rahim v. Malik Daud Khan and 6 others (2011 CLC 490), a Division Bench of this Court held that the function of the revenue offrcers is to prepare and maintain the revenue record, whereas the province of the civil Court is to determine civil rights and questions of title, and that a matter involving questions of fact requiring proof ought not to be disposed of summarily, but only after framing of issues and recording of evidence pro and contra. In Azad Khan and another v. Senior Member Board of Revenue, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 3 others (PLD 2019 Peshawar 208), it was held that the ouster of the civil Court's jurisdiction under Section 172 is confined to the precise powers defined therein, that the revenue authorities cannot circumvent the jurisdiction of a civil Court seized of a suit involving a question oftitle, and that the civil Court has the supervisory capacity to undo the effect ofany act performed by them. Likewise, in Shah Alam Khan and 2 others v. Board of Revenue, N.W.F.P. and 47 others (2020 YLR 2440), it was held, while relyins upon Muhammad Yousaf and 3 others v. Khan Bahadur through legal heirs (1992 SCMR 2334), that a Revenue (

(SB) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah KIan @ Officer cannot alter old settlement entries on the basis of which rights of other persons have been created, and that such a controversy, requiring evidence, can only be redressed by the civil Court.

8. The case in hand squarely falls within the ambit of the principles enunciated hereinabove. The petitioners seek to dislodge entries made in the settlement of L974-75, which have held the freld for about five decades and on the strength of which the respondents claim ownership. No Revenue Offrcer is competent to adjudicate upon such a dispute. Nor were the provisions of the Act of 1950 attracted at this stage. The respondents deny the petitioners'title and claim to be owners themselves, and the question whether any relationship of landlord and tenant exists between the parties at all is dependent upon the determination of title, which only the civil Court is competent to make. Sections 34-A and 35-A ofthe Act of 1950, relied upon by the learned Courts below, relate to a person whose ejectment has already been ordered or whose suit has been dismissed by a Revenue Court, and to a tenant seeking possession under Section 9 ofthe Specific Relief Act, 1877; neither situation arises in the present case. Moreover, the respective claims of the parties give rise to disputed questions offact which could not be resolved without framing of issues and recording of evidence. The power conferred by Order XV-A CPC is meant to be exercised only where no genuine triable issue arises from the pleadings; it is not a substitute for a regular trial where the controversy turns on contested facts. The suit, therefore, was not one fit for summary disposal under Order XV-A CPC.

(sB) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sabit Ullah Khan v 9. Both the learned Courts below, having treated the suit as one solely for correction of revenue entries, failed to exercise a jurisdiction vested in them by law within the contemplation of clause @)
of sub-section (1)

of Section 115 CPC, and thereby acted illegally and with material irregularity, warranting interference by this Court in the exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. Consequently, without dilating upon the merits of the case, Iest it prejudice the case of either party, this revision petition is allowed. The judgment and decree dated 23.10.2025 of the learned Additional District Judge-III, Karak, and the summary judgment and decree dated 07.12.2024 of the learned Civil Judge-fV, Karak, are hereby set aside, and the case is remanded to the learned trial Court, which shall, after framing of issues, recording of evidence pro and contra and hearing learned counsel for the parties, decide the suit afresh on its merits in accordance with law. Since the parties have been embroiled in litigation since the year 2021, the learned trial Court is expected to conclude the trial expeditiously.
Announced.
